fatal_errors: The proposed chromium-composition study does not reconstruct the central intervention: atmospheric-plasma-sprayed AlCoCrFeNi coating on SS316L followed by a 550 °C, 2 h anneal.
No prior findings or citations are supplied despite the explicit request for supporting evidence.
The proposed conditions omit the specified sulfuric-acid electrochemistry and 900 °C cyclic Na2SO4/NaCl/V2O5 hot-corrosion environments.
The hypothesis does not acknowledge that the target findings came from a subsequently retracted article.
explanation: The response offers a scientifically plausible and falsifiable general passivation hypothesis: chromium enrichment should produce a protective Cr-rich oxide and lower polarization current and mass loss relative to low-chromium controls. Its composition series, film characterization, and corrosion measurements could discriminate that hypothesis, although changing bulk chromium may also change microstructure and other alloy properties unless model alloys are carefully controlled. Agreement with the target is limited to the broad role of Cr-rich passive products and the prediction of reduced corrosion current. It misses the AlCoCrFeNi HEA coating, APS processing, annealing-temperature comparison, grain refinement and BCC/FCC mediator, Al/Cr-rich multicomponent scale, sluggish-diffusion claim, micropore-assisted salt ingress, and quantitative baselines. Its boundaries are stated only generically, and the absence of supporting evidence prevents satisfaction of the evidence requirement.
